pairs.evidence: crates/engine-wasm/wit/pumper-app.wit:18 The only embedded engine is wasmtime, which Pumper hosts rather than authors, and its guest world carries no filesystem, no clock and no job queue, so none of the six engine-side seams exists to judge (engine-claude is a subprocess, engine-search a tantivy index). Searched for HostHooks, JobExecutor, microtask, macrotask, ModuleLoader, rquickjs, boa_engine, deno_core, mlua, rhai and found none.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:1 Pumper is a host of wasmtime, not the author of an engine; it publishes no specification-mirrored override surface for embedders, only its own capability linker.
crates/engine-wasm/src/app_host.rs:15 The guest runs as a wasmtime async call on the host's tokio runtime; there is no guest job queue (promise reactions, timers) and so no executor seam to fill.
crates/engine-wasm/src/app_host.rs:15 Core wasm/component guests have no traced heap shared with host-queued jobs, so the traced-heap-plus-outside-queue window the technique governs does not exist.
crates/engine-wasm/src/app_host.rs:15 Each run is one awaited guest call with no timers or microtask queues to drain, which the technique's own when-not-to-use names as the case that needs no loop.

crates/engine-wasm/wit/pumper-app.wit:18 The guest has no filesystem and no module import of its own; the host loads .wasm by directory scan (crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:648), not by resolving a guest specifier against a referrer.
crates/engine-wasm/wit/pumper-app.wit:18 The WIT world exposes no clock to the guest, so there is no timer or date seam to split; the host's Instant use is its own wall-time ceiling.

pairs.registryProposal: engine-host-contract's use_when opens with 'embedding a language engine in a host', which literally matches a wasmtime host, but the body is written from the engine author's side and every technique assumes guest-visible jobs, a specifier loader or a guest clock. Add a scope line saying a host of a core-wasm/component engine with no guest event loop, imports or clock is out of scope (or name the host-side neighbour), so judges stop re-deriving the N/A.
